capability_ids._note: Reserved/disabled features live in a distinct identifier space, disjoint from every service_id (0-5), starting at 0x1001 (rework 1 fix after the validator caught a collision).

authorization_levels._note: Rework 2 review item 9: corrected from a single UNAUTHENTICATED==0-only check to an ordered policy. Phase 1 implements exactly one level (TRANSPORT_POSSESSION); higher levels are reserved so a stronger future level satisfies a weaker requirement (ordinal >= required, never ==).
authorization_levels.reserved_future_min_ordinal_note: Any operation requiring authorization_level >= N is satisfied by a presented level with ordinal >= N. Phase 1 defines only ordinal 0; every canonical opcode in this file requires ordinal 0 (the weakest/only defined level), so every Phase-1 adapter session (which authenticates only by transport possession) satisfies every operation's requirement.

lab_controls_policy._note: New, contract review 9 item 4. TRANSPORT_POSSESSION alone is not lab authorization -- every Phase-1 session has it by construction (authorization_levels above), so gating a diagnostic mode-override control on authorization_level alone would make it universally callable. A separate, explicit policy gate is required for any operation that lets a caller directly override the Wi-Fi driver mode outside a feature's own arbiter-owned transition.
lab_controls_policy.when_false: the gated operation reports capability_state DISABLED for every profile that would otherwise be SUPPORTED, and any request against it (bypassing capability discovery) is rejected the legal wire status UNSUPPORTED with no side effect -- mode is left completely unchanged, no partial state transition, no radio/arbiter interaction attempted. DISABLED is a capability-discovery state only, never a wire status (contract review 10 item 5); status_outcomes for the gated operation lists UNSUPPORTED, never DISABLED.
lab_controls_policy.when_true: ordinary authorization_level >= TRANSPORT_POSSESSION plus the operation's own atomic-lock BUSY/no-side-effect precondition checks (opcode lifecycle_meta) still apply in full -- the lab gate only removes the DISABLED capability-discovery default, it never substitutes for or weakens the other checks
lab_controls_policy.enablement_mechanism: a separately identified lab build/profile (a distinct compile-time configuration from the universal three-adapter customer/factory artifact, 002-compatibility-boundary-and-size-gate.md Sec 5.5) or a future authenticated administrative policy -- neither is an unauthenticated runtime toggle, and this task does not invent one
lab_controls_policy.opcode_stays_compiled_in: the canonical opcode remains compiled into the universal image and is truthfully capability-reported as DISABLED there (never removed/hidden); only a lab-enabled native build may report SUPPORTED for it -- WIFI_MODE_SET's bedge_c3 mapping remains DISABLED regardless of this gate, pending T-WIFI-5, since T-WIFI-5 (no dispatch case evidenced in any pinned build) is a wholly separate, unrelated gate that a lab-enabled Bedge build does not close (contract review 10 item 7)

opcodes.rc12_capability_correction: RC12 hardening round, item 5 (P1): native/bedge_c3 downgraded SUPPORTED -> UNSUPPORTED. This candidate wires no SNTP client, so a dispatched TIME_SYNC_START always terminates FAILED/IO_ERROR (handle_time_sync_start, mtek_system_logic.c). Advertising SUPPORTED was a dishonest capability claim kept alive only because several host tests borrowed this opcode as a generic arbiter-free ACCEPTED_ASYNC vehicle; those tests are decoupled onto a test-only overlay opcode (mtek_opcode_overlay.h / mtk_test_async_fixture) so the production advertisement can now tell the truth. factory_uart was already UNAVAILABLE (no diff). Restore to SUPPORTED only when a real SNTP implementation exists.

adapter_map.bedge_c3: 0x0009 M1_RPC_SYS_SNTP_SYNC (REQ none, WiFi must be up -> RESP m1_rpc_time_t{year:u16,month:u8,day:u8,hour:u8,minute:u8,second:u8,weekday:u8} or NAK). Bedge supports this START mapping only when the canonical request's server field is empty or exactly the literal 'pool.ntp.org' -- any other server value returns status=UNSUPPORTED before dispatch, with no operation token minted and no Bedge request ever sent, since the Bedge dispatch has no per-call server-selection wire field to carry a different value toward (contract review 9 item 3). RC12: superseded by the capability downgrade above -- native/bedge_c3 now report UNSUPPORTED for TIME_SYNC_START unconditionally until a real SNTP client exists.

opcodes.notes: List B -- clean-slate platform utility, classified 2026-09-04 (User Classification Decision / contract review 8 item 2, tasks/002_CANONICAL_SERVICE_CONTRACTS.md); not a shipped-customer parity surface, no List A preservation obligation. Precondition (own field, not a generic core rule): requires an already-connected station -- source-confirmed handle_sntp_sync checks wifi_mgr_is_connected() first and returns NAK(M1_RPC_ERR_NOT_RUNNING) if not connected; the canonical operation rejects with status=NOT_READY (no operation token minted) under the identical precondition, never attempting to bring Wi-Fi up itself. Malformed/out-of-bounds server or timeout_ms is rejected status=INVALID_ARGUMENT (no token minted); an already-active time sync (one in-flight TIME_SYNC_START per session) is rejected status=BUSY; operation-table exhaustion is rejected status=NO_MEMORY; a request against an unavailable profile (factory-UART, capability_state=UNAVAILABLE) or a rejected Bedge custom-server value (adapter_map above) reports the legal wire status UNSUPPORTED, no token minted -- UNAVAILABLE/DISABLED/UNSUPPORTED are capability-discovery states, not wire statuses, so status_outcomes never lists UNAVAILABLE (contract review 10 item 5). These five pre-acceptance outcomes and the four post-acceptance terminal outcomes (lifecycle_meta.terminal_outcomes above) are exact and exhaustive -- no IO_ERROR/NOT_READY ambiguity (contract review 9 item 2). Never changes Wi-Fi mode or credentials and owns no radio-mode lease (no_radio_lease:true) -- it rides on whatever station connection already exists, exactly like STA_STATUS. The request always encodes both fields on the wire (server is a bounded length-prefixed field whose zero length selects the configured/default pool; timeout_ms is an explicit u32 with no separate implicit timer) -- no optional-field encoding is invented; an API caller that omits timeout_ms sends the literal default 15000. Accepted timeout_ms range is exactly 1000..60000. The Bedge dispatch itself blocks synchronously up to 5000ms (esp_netif_sntp_sync_wait(pdMS_TO_TICKS(5000))) and always targets a hard-coded pool.ntp.org; the adapter therefore only honors a canonical server value of '' or 'pool.ntp.org' toward a Bedge peer (adapter_map above) and cannot honor any other value -- a genuine per-profile field-expressibility gap, not a byte assumption, named as adapter test T-SYS-2. Bedge's minimal m1_rpc_time_t carries no stratum/uncertainty figure at all; on a successful Bedge-sourced translation the adapter reports stratum=0 (UNSPECIFIED) and uncertainty_ms=0xFFFFFFFF (reserved sentinel meaning 'not reported by this profile', never a claim of perfect precision), named as the same adapter test T-SYS-2; all Bedge-sourced failure translations remain all-zero like every other non-success terminal payload. unix_time_ms is the adapter's own conversion of the calendar-form m1_rpc_time_t to milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC, matching the struct's own gmtime_r-sourced fields) -- an ordinary, lossless calendar-to-epoch conversion, not a wire fact requiring source evidence. Native/Bedge SUPPORTED for TIME_SYNC_START specifically; factory-UART UNAVAILABLE absent any evidenced factory time-sync console command. TIME_SYNC_STOP is a separate opcode with its own, different per-profile capability_state (see its own entry) -- the two time operations do not share one Bedge disposition (contract review 9 item 3).

opcodes.name: DEAUTH_START

lifecycle_meta.cleanup: radio released, STA mode restored; the entire selected/all/broadcast run is covered by exactly one operation token and one D-class lease

deauth_target_mode_invariants.SELECTED: station_scan_token=0; ap_bssid is one valid unicast AP BSSID; channel is 1..13; targets contains 1..64 unique valid unicast station MACs; empty, duplicate, multicast/broadcast, all-zero, or more-than-64 selections are rejected INVALID_ARGUMENT before the radio is acquired
deauth_target_mode_invariants.ALL_SCANNED: station_scan_token identifies one completed, still-retained STA_SCAN_START result (its STA_SCAN_COMPLETE result_generation) in the current boot/session; targets is empty; ap_bssid is all-zero and channel=0; at acceptance, the retained result's full unique station set plus its AP BSSID/channel is atomically copied into a private bounded snapshot, maximum 64; a missing/stale/wrong-session token returns NOT_FOUND; an in-progress or completed-empty scan returns NOT_READY; overflow beyond the retained 64-entry contract returns OVERFLOW; later cache changes cannot change an already-accepted operation's target set -- this is the exact native/factory 'deauth all' meaning: every station in the current completed station-scan table for the selected AP
deauth_target_mode_invariants.BROADCAST: station_scan_token=0; ap_bssid is one valid unicast AP BSSID; channel is 1..13; targets is empty; transmits to the broadcast station address (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) for that AP -- distinct from ALL_SCANNED even though both may affect all clients

lifecycle_meta.count_interval_rule: count=0 still means run until STOP; nonzero is the total frame-pair budget across the accepted snapshot, scheduled round-robin and deterministically capped; interval_ms=0 remains a safe implementation default, never a zero-delay loop

adapter_map.factory_uart: bare 'deauth' (no args) -> SELECTED, single target = the console's currently select -s'd station against the console's currently select -a'd AP (precondition: both selections done, else '[!] Invalid deauth target selection. Scan/select targets first.'); 'deauth set <id,id,...>' -> SELECTED, targets = the comma-listed station-table ids; 'deauth all' -> ALL_SCANNED against the current station-scan table; 'deauth broadcast' -> BROADCAST against the selected AP; malformed/unknown syntax -> '[!] Usage: deauth [set <id,id,...>|all|broadcast]' -- baseline grammar/selection errors preserved unchanged from 001-command-behavior-matrix.md lines 45-48
adapter_map.bedge_c3: 0x0302 M1ESP_OFF_DEAUTH_START, m1esp_deauth_req_t{bssid[6], channel, station[6], count, interval_ms} (references/bedge/M1OS/m1_csrc/m1_esp_rpc.h lines 352-359) -- source-evidenced as exactly one AP BSSID plus one station MAC per RPC, so a Bedge peer can express SELECTED (station = a specific client MAC) and BROADCAST (station = FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) but never ALL_SCANNED or a multi-target set in one RPC; this is a per-profile field-expressibility limit of the Bedge wire shape, not a missing deauth capability -- the Bedge/C3 UI's own specific-client-versus-'All (broadcast)' choice on one selected AP maps to native SELECTED versus BROADCAST, never to native ALL_SCANNED's per-scan station enumeration. Bedge source is design evidence only, not List A parity.

adapter_map.bedge_c3: 0x0101 M1_RPC_WIFI_SET_MODE (header REQ u8 mode; no dispatch case exists in any pinned main.c read this session and no enum-value table is defined anywhere in the pinned header for what a Bedge peer's own numeric 'mode' byte means -- capability-reported DISABLED pending T-WIFI-5, not SUPPORTED, independent of and in addition to the lab_controls_enabled gate below; canonical WifiMode numbering 0..3 above is this task's own clean-slate design, not assumed to match a Bedge peer's numbering without hardware confirmation)

opcodes.notes: List B -- clean-slate platform utility, classified 2026-09-04 (User Classification Decision / contract review 8 item 3). Synchronous, nonpersistent (persistent_effects:none, always volatile) diagnostic control. Corrected contract review 9 item 4: authorization.level >= TRANSPORT_POSSESSION (0) alone is NOT lab authorization -- every Phase-1 session has TRANSPORT_POSSESSION by construction (schemas.json authorization_levels), so that check alone would make this operation universally callable, not lab-gated. A real lab gate requires both ordinary TRANSPORT_POSSESSION authorization AND the separate, explicit lab_controls_enabled policy gate (schemas.json top-level lab_controls_policy), which defaults to false in the universal customer/factory artifact and is enabled only by a separately identified lab build/profile or a future authenticated administrative policy -- never an unauthenticated runtime toggle. When lab_controls_enabled is false, the operation returns the legal wire status UNSUPPORTED with no side effect at all (mode left completely unchanged, no arbiter interaction attempted) -- DISABLED is a capability-discovery state only, never a wire status (contract review 10 item 5; status_outcomes above lists UNSUPPORTED, never DISABLED); this is why capability_state.native above is DISABLED for the universal build; the canonical opcode remains compiled into the universal image and is truthfully capability-reported as DISABLED there, never removed or hidden. A lab-enabled native build may report SUPPORTED for this opcode; capability_state.bedge_c3 remains DISABLED regardless of the lab gate, per its own adapter_map note above, since T-WIFI-5 is a wholly separate, unrelated gate that a lab-enabled Bedge build does not close (contract review 10 item 7 -- no lab-enabled Bedge build ever reports this opcode SUPPORTED while T-WIFI-5 remains open). When lab_controls_enabled is true: mode accepts only OFF=0/STA=1/AP=2/APSTA=3; MONITOR=4 is a recognized, named enum value that is unconditionally rejected UNSUPPORTED (never INVALID_ARGUMENT, distinguishing a known-but-forbidden value from a malformed byte, which remains INVALID_ARGUMENT for any value outside 0..4) -- this operation must never bypass a feature-owned monitor/raw-radio transition (002-resource-arbiter.md), which is why MONITOR can never be entered through it. Executes through the core resource arbiter under one atomic control lock: rechecks there is no active radio lease (any WMC/WS/BEACON/D/H/M/SAP/RAW class holder), no active STA connection, and no active SoftAP; if any of those holds, returns BUSY with no side effect at all (previous_mode/applied_mode both omitted from meaning -- response is the BUSY status alone, mode is left completely unchanged). On success returns {previous_mode, applied_mode} (applied_mode always equals the requested mode on OK); creates no new concurrency and acquires no lease of its own (no_radio_lease:true, momentary control-plane check only).
